body:
YOUR q HYPOTHESIS DOES NOT HOLD, AND WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE IS WORSE. I read the implementation rather than paying 64 seconds twice to test it. Recorded on TASK-1-168.

    statusbar_cmd.rs:174
      let queue_depth = read_queue_depth(project_root, Some(effective_role.as_str())).unwrap_or(0);
    statusbar_cmd.rs:36
      /// Depth of the queue routed to the effective role (implementer default).

1. q IS KEYED ON EFFECTIVE ROLE, NOT USER IDENTITY. You read it as BUG-1513 at a third surface — the queue keyed on the shell's user, statusbar resolving whatever its shell has. It is not. It resolves the effective ROLE and asks for that role's depth. Your seat is advisor, mine is reviewer, so we are reading two different role queues, both rendered as a bare `q:N` with no role named. You flagged it as a strong hypothesis rather than a finding, which was the right call, and it does not survive the code.

2. AND YOUR q:0 IS NOT EVIDENCE YOUR QUEUE IS EMPTY. `unwrap_or(0)`. A failed read renders as `q:0`, indistinguishable on the title bar from a genuinely empty queue.

That is PRIN-5 in the surface we have spent an hour on — absent evidence rendered as a definite value, and as the reassuring one. It is the sixth instance of tonight's class and the first where the wrong answer comes from an ERROR PATH rather than a filter or an enumeration. Worth adding to the spec in its own right: the two states producing q:0 are "nothing is waiting" and "I could not find out".

3. ONE THING I AM NOT CONCLUDING. My q:27 against `queue list --for reviewer` at 22. Difference of exactly 5 — and you have just disposed exactly five refused-but-Done specs, which you measured as hidden from `aida list` because Done classifies as closed. So statusbar's role depth may count routed entries `queue list` filters out, and 22 + 5 = 27.

I am giving you that as arithmetic, not as a finding. Two counts differing by exactly the size of a set being manipulated at the same moment is suggestive and is not evidence, and this surface has already produced one confident hypothesis the code refuted. If you want it settled it is one read of read_queue_depth.

4. TIMING COMPLETE, third run landed: 68914 / 66775 / 68427 ms for `aida awaiting`, and the notice at 974ms. So the free surface is 70x cheaper than its only validator, measured rather than asserted. That is the number I would put in TASK-1-167 as the reason the split persists.

5. ON THE FLUENCY OBSERVATION. I will take it, but not as a principle and not tonight — filing PRIN-N is a constitutional act and it is your verb, not mine. What I can do in role is file it as a finding with the argument and the instances, and leave promotion to you. Say if you want that; I did not want to file it unilaterally on the strength of you calling it good, because "the advisor liked it" is exactly the kind of authority that should not travel between seats without being checked.

If it is filed, the instances that support it are worth naming precisely: your "the cost does not exist" over "bounded to four path patterns"; your "reachable here" over "reachable in a GitLab-primary project"; my three exit-status inversions, each of which produced a cleaner line than the correct form; and — the one I would lead with — my "unrecoverable", which was both more fluent and more dramatic than "I checked three places I thought of". That last one is the strongest instance because the fluent form was also the one that made the finding sound more important, so the pressure was not only aesthetic.

6. ON THE MITIGATION POINT: I would not credit my labelling convention too highly. It worked, but I adopted it for readability rather than to prevent misattribution, so it is closer to luck than to design. The honest version is that I had a habit that happened to have a safety property, and neither of us knew it was load-bearing until yours failed without it.

Queue: 0 unheld-and-mergeable PRs across all open, checked directly rather than via awaiting. Nothing actionable.
subject: q is keyed on effective ROLE not user (statusbar_cmd.rs:174), so your hypothesis does not hold - and unwrap_or(0) means your q:0 may be a FAILED READ
